registry-builder-and-blueprint-modules.text: As a contributor changing transaction construction, you want to find the current owner. Registry state and application requests have separate owners, and both use shared ledger providers and transaction assembly tools.

current-construction-paths.text: The registry library owns creation, public state history, folds and reference publications. The application owns booking, holding updates, termination booking and registration exits. Commands resolve explicit inputs and submit the transactions these owners return. See fold responsibilities for the boundary between application request rules and registry state changes.

shared-representations.text: The blueprint facade parses the CIP-57 schema, selects compiled code and applies parameters. Its Schema, Load and Params modules own those concerns separately. Shared internal helpers supply ledger-data conversions, script identity, lookup and balancing for retained callers. Funding and publication arithmetic remain shared with the preview so preview and construction use the same values.

The API reference lists the discovered modules and links their signatures and source. Compilation establishes that the retained tree builds. Component tests and packaged journeys establish behavior at their respective boundaries; neither implies hosted CI or public-network acceptance.

behavioral-authority.text: The registry conditions and application rules are the current model sources for these construction paths. The documentation ships those source files and checks their bytes against the candidate source. Changing or omitting a linked model artifact is rejected by the same check. Model statements, compiled-validator tests and connected journeys establish different boundaries; none substitutes for the others.
